guarantees.claim: reseed_cnt increments by 1 every clock cycle when (cnt_en & lfsr_en_i) is high, and is cleared to 0 when edn_done is high. The counter immediately exposes its value (commit_i=1). No decrement or set capability is enabled.

formal.consequent: if (edn_done) reseed_cnt' == 0 else if (cnt_en && lfsr_en_i) reseed_cnt' == reseed_cnt + 1 else reseed_cnt' == reseed_cnt

formal_sketch.consequent: if (edn_done) reseed_cnt' == 0 else if (cnt_en && lfsr_en_i) reseed_cnt' == reseed_cnt + 1 else reseed_cnt' == reseed_cnt

guarantees.claim: cnt_err_o is directly forwarded from the prim_count error output without any local masking or gating.
cnt_after_commit_o output is left unconnected; its value is unused within the module.

assumptions.claim: External logic must not assert (cnt_en & lfsr_en_i) continuously for more than 65535 cycles; otherwise the counter overflows and wraps.
assumptions.risk: Counter overflow causes reseed_cnt wrap, potentially bypassing reseed scheduling and compromising key freshness.

assumptions.claim: edn_done must be a clean pulse and must not be stuck high; else the counter remains cleared and reseeding may never occur.
assumptions.risk: If edn_done stays high, reseed_cnt stays at 0, potentially freezing reseed logic.

uncertain_points.claim: cnt_err_o is not evaluated locally; a counter overflow (e.g., when cnt_en & lfsr_en_i stay high for >65535 cycles) would propagate to the outside world without any containment in this chunk.
uncertain_points.risk: If external logic ignores cnt_err_o, overflow could go undetected, allowing a reseed count wrap and violating reseed frequency requirements, potentially compromising key material freshness.

formal_sketch.consequent: cnt_err_o is not evaluated locally; a counter overflow (e.g., when cnt_en & lfsr_en_i stay high for >65535 cycles) would propagate to the outside world without any containment in this chunk

uncertain_points.cond: if commit_i is changed from constant 1
uncertain_points.risk: Potential functional gap if commit_i later becomes a dynamic signal and the delayed-commit feature is needed.

security_implications: The counter reseed_cnt (16‑bit) increments on lfsr_en_i & cnt_en and clears on edn_done. If extraneous continuous assertion of the enable signals causes overflow, cnt_err_o may be asserted and reseed_cnt wraps. Without local containment (cnt_err_o is only forwarded, not gated or handled here), an overflow could allow an attacker to force the reseed count to wrap, potentially missing reseeding intervals and exposing stale key material. The error path relies entirely on external logic for fault handling, which creates a security‑critical dependency.
